title: Last derivative at an appended point
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. For every bit $b$ and every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the discrete derivative of $f$ in the last coordinate at the point obtained by appending $b$ to $x$ equals the last-coordinate half-difference of $f$ at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean hypercube
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, and $d=(f_0-f_1)/2$. Then $D_n f(x,b)=d(x)$ for all $x$ and $b$, where $D_n$ is the last-coordinate half-difference.
